module purpose: neorv32_cpu_cp_cfu holds four 32-bit key words that are written and read through a CSR port (csr_we_i, csr_addr_i, csr_wdata_i, csr_rdata_o). When start_i is '1' with rtype_i equal to r3type_c, it captures two operands from rs1_i and rs2_i. One cycle later it updates a running sum (load, add or subtract a constant) and registers a result computed from the operands, the sum and a key word indexed by the sum, as chosen by funct3_i. It reports the result on result_o and completion on valid_o.

use-case flows.value: a 32-bit key word taken from csr_wdata_i into the key_mem word indexed by csr_addr_i when csr_we_i is '1'
the key_mem word indexed by csr_addr_i, driven on csr_rdata_o
operation request: when start_i is '1' and rtype_i equals r3type_c, rs1_i and rs2_i are captured as operands and the pending flag xtea.done(0) is set
running sum: loaded from the first operand, or increased or decreased by the constant xtea_delta_c, as funct3_i chooses, one cycle after the request
result word: operands, running sum and the key word indexed by sum bits are combined by shifts, additions and XORs, then added to or subtracted from an operand and registered in xtea.res
result and completion: xtea.done(0) is delayed into xtea.done(1); result_o and valid_o are selected by rtype_i and funct3_i from xtea.res, xtea.done(1) or constants
key words, operands, sum, result and completion flags cleared to zero while rstn_i is '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Stored key words -- the four 32-bit words written over the CSR port, read back on it, and mixed into each result as the word indexed by the running sum
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: `key_mem(to_integer(unsigned(csr_addr_i))) <= csr_wdata_i;` (line 179, under `if (csr_we_i = '1')`, line 178) stores the word. The word is held between writes and cleared only by reset (line 176). Operate flow: tmp_z takes the key_mem word indexed by xtea.sum bits (lines 236-237). tmp_z feeds tmp_r (line 238), and tmp_r feeds xtea.res (lines 222, 224). A corrupted word changes every result computed with it, so Integrity is Established. Read out: `csr_rdata_o <= key_mem(to_integer(unsigned(csr_addr_i)));` (line 185) delivers the word across the boundary, so the requester must receive exactly the stored word. Availability is Established for holding: the word persists from its write until the next write to the same index or until reset. Confidentiality is not established: line 185 returns any word on csr_rdata_o with no condition, and no line restricts who observes it. key_mem stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, line 179). csr_wdata_i sets it, because this entity reads csr_wdata_i to store the word (CARRIES key_mem, occurrence 2, line 179). csr_rdata_o is an exit port (DERIVES_FROM key_mem, occurrence 2, line 185). The CSR ports are plain vectors and scalars, not a record carrying complete transactions, so the transport rule does not apply. tmp_z only selects a word on its way into the computation (DERIVES_FROM key_mem, line 236) and is not a reference. csr_we_i and csr_addr_i decide the write; they are reported under the write-control concept.

conceptual assets.concept: Key-word write control -- whether a CSR access replaces a stored key word, and which of the four words it replaces
conceptual assets.reasoning: `if (csr_we_i = '1') then` (line 178) followed by `key_mem(to_integer(unsigned(csr_addr_i))) <= csr_wdata_i;` (line 179): the write lands only when csr_we_i is '1', and only in the word indexed by csr_addr_i. A wrong enable or index overwrites a different word or skips the write, which breaks the configure flow, so Integrity is Established. Availability holds under the implemented conditions: with rstn_i at '1' and csr_we_i at '1' at a rising edge of clk_i (line 177), the indexed word updates. csr_we_i sets the write decision (GATES key_mem, occurrence 2, line 178). csr_addr_i sets the word index (SELECTS key_mem, occurrence 2, line 179); it also selects the read-out word (SELECTS csr_rdata_o, occurrence 3, line 185). No internal element computes this decision: it is evaluated inline in the process.

conceptual assets.concept: Captured operands -- the two 32-bit operand words taken in when an operation is requested
conceptual assets.reasoning: Start flow: `xtea.opa <= rs1_i;` and `xtea.opb <= rs2_i;` (lines 205-206) run under `if (start_i = '1') and (rtype_i = r3type_c)` (line 204). The operands feed tmp_a, tmp_b, tmp_x and tmp_y (lines 232-235), then tmp_r (line 238) and xtea.res (lines 222, 224). xtea.opa also loads the running sum when funct3_i(2) is '1' (line 214). A corrupted operand changes the computed result, so Integrity is Established. Availability: the operands are held from capture until the next accepted request or reset (lines 194-195). xtea.opa and xtea.opb store them (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, lines 205 and 206). rs1_i and rs2_i set them, because this entity reads them to store them (CARRIES xtea.opa, occurrence 2, line 205; CARRIES xtea.opb, occurrence 2, line 206). The tmp_* signals only select or shift the operands on their way into the computation, so they are not references. start_i and rtype_i gate the capture; they are reported under the request concept. The file instantiates no sub-unit, so the sub-unit wiring rule does not apply to these fields.

conceptual assets.concept: Running sum state -- the 32-bit value loaded from an operand and then increased or decreased by a fixed constant; it indexes the key word and enters each result
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow, under `if (xtea.done(0) = '1')` (line 211): `xtea.sum <= xtea.opa;` when funct3_i(2) is '1' (line 214); the sum plus xtea_delta_c (line 216); the sum minus xtea_delta_c (line 218). The map lists xtea.sum as self-updating. Its bits 1-0 or 12-11 select the key word (SELECTS tmp_z, lines 236-237). Its value also enters `tmp_r <= ... xor std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(xtea.sum) + unsigned(tmp_z));` (line 238). A corrupted sum selects a different key word and changes every later result, so Integrity is Established. Availability: the sum is held between updates and changes only on the three listed arms or on reset (line 196). xtea.sum stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 216). funct3_i chooses the update arm (GATES xtea.sum, line 213); it is reported under the request concept. xtea.opa supplies the load value (CARRIES xtea.sum, line 214); it is reported under the operands concept.

conceptual assets.concept: Operation result -- the 32-bit word computed from the operands, the sum and a key word, registered and delivered on result_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow: `xtea.res <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(tmp_b) + unsigned(tmp_r));` (line 222), or the subtraction (line 224). funct3_i(1) chooses between them (line 221), xtea.done(0) enables them (line 211), and tmp_r comes from line 238. Report flow: `result_o <= xtea.res;` (line 249) when rtype_i equals r3type_c (line 245) and funct3_i is one of the four non-init codes (line 248); otherwise result_o is zero (lines 252, 255, 261). The result leaves through an output port to a consumer that is not supplied here. Its integrity property, that the consumer receives exactly the value lines 222-224 and 238 define, is therefore Established from line 249. Availability holds under the implemented conditions: after an accepted request (line 204), with reset inactive, the result is registered one rising edge later and held until the next update. xtea.res stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, line 222); this takes precedence over its computing role (DERIVES_FROM tmp_r at the same line). result_o is an exit port (COPIES xtea.res, occurrence 2, line 249). tmp_a, tmp_b, tmp_x, tmp_y, tmp_z and tmp_r are parts of the computation whose result is stored in xtea.res, not additional references.

conceptual assets.concept: Operation request -- whether an operation is accepted, and which function it performs (sum load, increase or decrease; add or subtract; operand order; what is reported)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Start flow: `if (start_i = '1') and (rtype_i = r3type_c) then` (line 204) decides whether operands are captured and the pending flag is set (lines 205-207). Operate and report flows: funct3_i chooses the sum update (lines 213-218), add or subtract for the result (lines 221-224), and the operand order and key-word index bits (lines 232-237). Together with rtype_i (line 245), it also chooses what result_o and valid_o report (lines 247-256). A wrong decision starts a spurious operation, skips a requested one, or performs a different function, so Integrity of the implemented operation is Established. start_i sets the decision (GATES xtea.done, occurrence 2, line 204). rtype_i sets it (GATES xtea.done, occurrence 2, line 204); it also gates result_o and valid_o (GATES, occurrence 4, line 245). funct3_i sets it (GATES xtea.sum, occurrence 2, line 213); it also selects result_o and valid_o (SELECTS, occurrence 12, line 247). No internal element computes this decision: it is evaluated inline. funct7_i, rs3_i and active_i have no local use, so they take no part.

conceptual assets.concept: Operation completion status -- the pending and done flags that mark an accepted request and a result ready one cycle later, reported on valid_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: `xtea.done(0) <= '1';` on an accepted request (line 207), otherwise '0' (line 200); then `xtea.done(1) <= xtea.done(0);` (line 201). xtea.done(0) enables the sum and result updates (line 211). xtea.done(1) is high in the cycle after them, when xtea.res holds the new result. `valid_o <= xtea.done(1);` (line 250) reports it for the four non-init codes; valid_o is '1' for the init code (line 253) and '0' otherwise (lines 256, 262). valid_o goes to a consumer that is not supplied here, so the consumer must receive exactly this flag. A corrupted flag reports an unfinished or stale result as valid, or hides a finished one, so Integrity is Established. Availability holds under the implemented conditions: one rising edge after an accepted request, with reset inactive, done(1) is produced. xtea.done stores the status (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 6, line 207; the map lists it as self-updating). valid_o is an exit port (DERIVES_FROM xtea.done, occurrence 2, line 250). start_i and rtype_i gate line 207; they are reported under the request concept. clk_i and rstn_i drive SEQUENCES and RESETS, so they are excluded as clock and reset.
